newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE CANOLA ENDS UP, BARLEY LIMIT UP ON CBOT CORN.
newsitem.headline: WCE CANOLA ENDS UP, BARLEY LIMIT UP ON CBOT CORN.

text.p: Winnipeg Commodity Exchange canola ended up $3.90 to $7.40 a tonne as funds bought and Cargill and hedgers were noted sellers, traders said.
"Funds bought 750 to 1,000 November through RBC-DS, Cargill sold 400 Nov, 100 Jan and there were 175 hedges in the November," a trader said.
November WCE canola crush profit margin fell to -20.78 Tuesday from -19.87 Monday. Nov-Jan spread at $4, Sep-Nov $3. Volume was 2,865 lots.
August canola closed $7.40 higher at $362 and November up ended up $4.40 at $361.40.
November flax ended $3.60 higher at $293.80 as speculators bought from commission houses. Sep-Nov spread at $12.
October western barley jumped the $5 limit to end at $137.10 and December was up $5 at $139.20 -- both following the lead set by CBOT corn futures which soared up the 12-cent-a-bushel limit.
The limit gains came after USDA early Tuesday estimated U.S. corn output at 9.276 billion bushels, well below expectations of 9.554 billion.
Alberta Wheat Pool and RBC-DS sold western barley to commercials and commission houses, traders said. Volume was 475 lots. Dec-Mar spread at $22.10.
October feed wheat rose the $5 limit to $160.20 and December climbed $5 to end at $160, buoyed by the gains in barley and corn with AWP selling, traders said.
Mar-May feed wheat spread at $0.10, Oct-Dec even money. Volume was 500. Oats did not trade.
UGG sold October peas up US$1.70 to US$170.50 to LFG, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except oats, feed peas.)
